thread.title: Real-Time Portfolio Strategies: Don't Back Test, Forward Test

author: On
title: Real-Time Portfolio Strategies: Don't Back Test, Forward Test
text: Real-Time Portfolio Strategies: Don't Back Test, Forward Test on Email Other Apps Two years ago, we began investing in spinoffs, achieving more than satisfactory returns of 31% in 2016 and 24.7% in 2017. We've continued with spinoffs in 2018 (by adding to current holdings) and we expect to keep a large portion of our portfolio in spinoffs going forward. However, we've learned a thing or three over the last two years and will no longer be adding shares to our portfolio simply because they're a spinoff. We've spent quite some time reverse engineering our most successful spinoffs, and are applying our proprietary ranking and weighting algorithm to all future spinoffs. This new approach may mean slim pickin's going forward. For that reason, the other portion of our portfolio will focus on a variety of investing strategies and measure them using the S&P 500 as our benchmark. By now you're probably thinking, with the possibility of generating over 20% in spinoffs over time, why not just stay 100% in generic spinoff situations? You're right. We should, but we'd be bored silly and have nothing to blog about. You're probably going to say; paper trade, or use computer simulations to back test any new strategies before committing capital. Again, you'd be right, but we aren't psychologically equipped to be happy using simulated results when testing an investment strategy. You see, we want "skin in the game". When we come up with a new strategy, we want a 'real-time' learning environment. We believe people make totally different investing decisions when using real money versus paper trading. At T9Z, we eat our own cooking. It's one thing to say your strategy beat the benchmark 17 out of 20 years "theoretically", but it's an entirely different thing to just do it. Besides, it's only money. With that administrivia out of the way, let's preview the first of our newest investment portfolios. We're calling it the "Rise of the Machines" Portfolio. We're identifying players in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Computer/Machine Vision. Opportunities here are further analyzed for investment potential using a blend of Buffett, Greenblatt, Munger, and Smith screening and valuation techniques. Our first two holdings are Apple (AAPL) and Intel (INTC). We expect the portfolio to be build up to about 6 to 9 holdings over the long term. Additional portfolio strategies include; Masters of the Universe, Negative Nellies, Safe Space Retreat, and Wag the Dog. The ultimate goal of each strategy is to beat the benchmark S&P 500, but we're also curious to see how they'll rank against our primary Vintage T9Z Spinoff Portfolio. Astute readers will notice a single stock can be a part of multiple strategies. Stay tuned as we'll introduce each one over the coming weeks.
